- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing upside reversal.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or 10% below true peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to continue falling; add 2–5% upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period momentum; add 2–5% upward adjustment for final 5–7 days if sentiment turns positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., negative → positive → negative), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for early reversal signals.
